title: ULIP Overview and Government Systems
text:
The Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) serves as a unified digital gateway for logistics-related data from multiple government systems through API-based integration. A July 2026 PIB release states that ULIP connects 46 government systems across 12 Central Ministries and Departments through 142 APIs and covers more than 2,000 data fields. The release says the platform has enabled more than 260 applications and more than 450 crore API transactions.

The same release describes ULIP as supp

The same release describes ULIP as supporting transparency, logistics efficiency, operational visibility, inter-departmental coordination and data-driven decision-making. The platform is used to enable seamless exchange of logistics data across departments and to support industry, MSMEs, exporters and other logistics stakeholders.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP Surpasses 100 Crore API Transactions
text: The Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) reached 100 crore API transactions in March 2025. The PIB release presents ULIP as a digital infrastructure initiative supporting technology-driven logistics and ease of doing business. The milestone is described as evidence of increasing use of API integrations by logistics stakeholders and government departments.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: HPCL Integration with ULIP
text:
HPCL signed an agreement with NICDC Logistics Data Services Ltd. to integrate APIs with the Unified Logistics Interface Platform. The HPCL API provides fuel-station and pricing visibility, including information about the location and pricing of HPCL fuel stations across India.

The PIB release explains that this kind of data can help logistics service providers, traders and transporters plan operations, improve visibility and reduce inefficiencies. The release describes ULIP as a digital gateway

title: ULIP Initial Design and Integration
text:
ULIP was designed as a platform for data exchange among operators across modes of transport. At the time of this PIB release, the platform had been integrated with 24 systems of six ministries through 78 APIs, including systems associated with ports, railways, road transport and highways, civil aviation, foreign trade and customs.

The release describes the objective as enabling access to data available with government systems for logistics and supporting more efficient movement of goods.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: National Logistics Policy 2022 — Summary
text:
The National Logistics Policy 2022 was notified for implementation in September 2022. The policy explains that logistics efficiency depends on infrastructure, services such as digital systems, processes and regulatory frameworks, and human resources.

The policy distinguishes the role of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan and the National Logistics Policy. PM GatiShakti focuses on integrated infrastructure and network planning for multimodal connectivity, while the National Logistics Policy addr
source: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade / Government of India

title: National Logistics Policy 2022 — Summary
text:
k planning for multimodal connectivity, while the National Logistics Policy addresses efficiency in services, processes, digital systems, regulatory frameworks and human resources.

The policy seeks an integrated, technologically enabled, cost-efficient, resilient, sustainable and trusted logistics ecosystem. It is intended to support smoother movement of goods and improve logistics performance.
source: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade / Government of India

title: National Logistics Policy — DPIIT Overview
text:
The National Logistics Policy (NLP) was launched on 17 September 2022 to complement the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan. The DPIIT overview says PM GatiShakti addresses integrated development of fixed infrastructure and network planning, while NLP addresses soft infrastructure and logistics-sector development including process reforms, improvement in logistics services, digitization, human-resource development and skilling.

The stated aim of NLP 2022 is to develop a technologically enabled,
source: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade

title: National Logistics Policy — DPIIT Overview
text:

The stated aim of NLP 2022 is to develop a technologically enabled, integrated, cost-efficient, resilient, sustainable and trusted logistics ecosystem for accelerated and inclusive growth. Its vision is to drive economic growth and business competitiveness through an integrated, seamless, efficient, reliable, green, sustainable and cost-effective logistics network using technology, processes and skilled manpower.
source: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade

title: ULIP and National Logistics Policy Relationship
text:
The Prime Minister launched the National Logistics Policy on 17 September 2022. The PIB release describes the policy as a driving and guiding force for logistics and states that the National Logistics Policy and GatiShakti are intended to work together to improve India's logistics ecosystem.

The policy launch material emphasizes reducing logistics costs, improving efficiency, ending departmental silos and supporting trade and stakeholders. ULIP is part of the broader digital and data-integratio

title: ULIP 2023 Progress
text:
The 2023 DPIIT year-end review reported that ULIP had been integrated with 35 systems of eight ministries through 113 APIs and covered more than 1,800 fields. The review also reported 699 industry players registered on ULIP, more than 125 private companies that had signed NDAs, and more than 65 applications live.

The review said GST data was being integrated with ULIP to support end-to-end multimodal tracking of cargo and demand-supply mapping for trade.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP and Logistics Visibility
text: A Government of India logistics publication describes ULIP as a digital platform that brings together data from logistics-related ministries and departments through a single interface. It notes that ULIP reached 100 crore API transactions in March 2025 and describes ULIP as supporting shipment ETAs and logistics visibility.
source: Press Information Bureau / Government of India publication

title: ULIP Historical Context
text: ULIP was designed by NICDC under the guidance of NITI Aayog as a platform for data exchange among transport-mode operators. Early integrations included government systems from ports, shipping, railways, road transport, civil aviation, foreign trade and customs. The project was intended to make government logistics data accessible through APIs for stakeholders.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP and Green Logistics
text:
A July 2024 PIB release describes sustainable logistics as important for economic growth and environmental well-being. It says that the National Logistics Policy promotes digital technology adoption and that NICDC has developed ULIP and the Logistics Data Bank for digital tracking and monitoring of logistics movement.

The release says ULIP and the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan support data-driven decision-making. At the time of the release, ULIP provided industry users secure access to log
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP and Green Logistics
text:
g. At the time of the release, ULIP provided industry users secure access to logistics data held by multiple ministries, with 37 systems from ten ministries integrated through 118 APIs and more than 1,800 data fields.

It also describes policy measures for sustainable logistics, including multimodal transport, digitalization and automation. A Freight Greenhouse Gas Calculator is described as a tool for comparing transport costs and greenhouse-gas emissions for a fixed origin-destination pair.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP API Access and Logistics Digitization
text:
A December 2024 PIB reply describes ULIP as a digital gateway that enables industry stakeholders to access logistics-related datasets from government systems through API-based integration. It says ULIP operates on a request-response mechanism.

The reply reported that ULIP was integrated with 39 systems of 11 ministries, providing access to more than 1,800 data fields through 125 APIs at that point in time. It places ULIP alongside freight digitization, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks, air-cargo fac
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP API Access and Logistics Digitization
text:
ULIP alongside freight digitization, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks, air-cargo facilities and the Logistics Data Bank as initiatives expected to reduce logistics costs, improve transit times and improve supply-chain efficiency.

The same source says the Logistics Data Bank uses RFID technology to provide real-time tracking of India’s containerized EXIM cargo. It also notes that the Freight Greenhouse Gas Calculator compares emissions and transport costs for a fixed origin-destination pair.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP and Logistics Data Bank 2.0
text:
A November 2025 PIB backgrounder says ULIP integrates data across departments, while Logistics Data Bank (LDB) 2.0 provides real-time visibility of containers. It describes these platforms as part of a data-driven logistics ecosystem alongside policy reforms and multimodal infrastructure.

The source says LDB 2.0 synchronizes with ULIP APIs to offer exporters and MSMEs visibility across road, rail, sea and high seas. It states that users can track shipments through container number, vehicle numb
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP and Logistics Data Bank 2.0
text:
It states that users can track shipments through container number, vehicle number and railway Freight Name Record (FNR) number, and that a live container heatmap can surface delays.

The backgrounder also explains that the National Logistics Policy and PM GatiShakti support an integrated, data-driven logistics ecosystem intended to reduce costs and improve efficiency.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: Sagar Setu, FOIS and ULIP Integration
text:
A Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways PIB reply explains that Sagar Setu supports real-time data exchange for importers, exporters, customs brokers and freight forwarders. It reports that Sagar Setu had integration with major and non-major ports and that the platform supports several port-related activities.

The source says Sagar Setu messages are integrated with the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS) for information including voyage registration, electronic verified gross mass,
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

text:
) for information including voyage registration, electronic verified gross mass, berth allotment and container or bulk pendency. It also says that multiple messages are integrated between ULIP and Sagar Setu.

The reply further describes ICEGATE integration as streamlining electronic data exchange between customs and ports. This document supports questions about the role of port, customs and rail systems in multimodal logistics.
source: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

title: ULIP Use Cases and Integrated Systems
text:
The DPIIT Annual Report 2023–24 describes ULIP as an API-based integration platform for logistics systems across government departments. It reports historical progress of integration with 35 systems across eight ministries through 116 APIs, covering more than 1,800 fields.

The report lists examples of private-sector use cases: track and trace, gate automation, financing and payments for transporters, green or sustainable logistics, process digitization, e-KYC and verification, third-party trans

title: Vahan, Sarathi and FASTag Services
text:
A Ministry of Road Transport and Highways PIB release describes Vahan and Sarathi as the two flagship applications of the Transport Mission Mode Project. It says Vahan covers vehicle registration, taxation, permits, fitness and related services. Sarathi covers driving licences, learner licences, driving schools and related services.

The source describes FASTag as an electronic toll-collection mechanism used at fee plazas. It says the initiative supports digital toll payment and smoother passage
source: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

title: Vahan, Sarathi and FASTag Services
text:
lazas. It says the initiative supports digital toll payment and smoother passage through toll plazas, and discusses wider adoption of FASTag for road users.

In a logistics context, Vahan-style vehicle-registration information can support vehicle verification and gate automation, while FASTag events can support movement visibility. This final statement is an application-level interpretation; access to data remains governed by the relevant platform and authorization processes.
